idiom_name: module of async functions (or small class) over fetch/Undici with a Map cache
implementation_notes: Runtimes ship fetch (Node uses Undici underneath), so the delegate collapses into a module exporting exactly the operations the client needs: each function builds the request, calls fetch with a base URL and default headers, checks response.ok and throws an application-level error, while a module-level Map or LRU caches idempotent results. What replaces the classic structure: no delegate class and no lookup component - endpoint configuration and credentials are module state, and the module boundary provides the hiding. A class (closure with injected transport) is still worth it when the delegate needs per-tenant state or must be substituted in tests.
pitfalls: fetch rejects only on network failure; HTTP 4xx/5xx are successful resolutions, so response.ok must be checked or errors flow silently into the view.
There is no default timeout: use AbortSignal.timeout()/AbortController or a hung remote call pins the request indefinitely.
A module-level Map is unbounded and per-process; cap it (LRU/TTL) and key it on tenant/auth data or cached responses leak across users.
